newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulls multi-service accounts for brokerages.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulls multi-service accounts for brokerages.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Tuesday that it was mulling the possibility of allowing Japanese securities houses to start offering multi-service accounts as part of its planned "Big Bang" financial reforms.
A ministry official told Reuters that an advisory panel to the finance minister has been debating the issue and would likely reach a conclusion by June at the latest.

"The panel could reach a conclusion on the issue before June," the official said. "Based on the panel's conclusion, the ministry will review the issue and take swift action depending on the outcome," the official added.
"The issue of multi-service accounts is now under discussion from a view point of how brokerages can diversify and improve their services," the ministry official said, without specifying details.
The mass daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday that MOF would allow brokerages to start offering multi-service accounts in the fiscal year from April 1.

The accounts allow customers to automatically transfer profits from stock sales to a money management fund (MMF), a type of short-term bond management trust, and to trust funds investing mainly in medium-term government notes.
Customers' credit card charges and public utility fees can also be paid from the accounts, the newspaper said.
But the newspaper added that banks, which currently offer similar multi-functional accounts, might be opposed to allowing brokerages to have the accounts. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9404
